gen-archivo-black-gf-faustina: Authoritative and urban, Archivo Black fills the middle of every line with heavy, spacious letters. And Faustina, a serif with gently thinning bowls, carries the text with a quiet, bookish rhythm down the page.
gen-fs-red-hat-display-plus-jakarta-sans: Red Hat Display draws bold, marker-like lines with visible daylight inside every curve, giving headings a confident, contemporary punch. Plus Jakarta Sans handles the quieter work.
gen-fs-oswald-gf-rokkitt: Oswald packs its rows tightly, strong and confident. Shrink it down, though, and Rokkitt, a serif with a wide-open c, starts to steal the attention.
gen-archivo-black-gf-halant: Halant brings a faint thick-thin shift and tall, outward-pointing terminals to the text. Archivo Black simply hits harder.
gen-fs-oswald-gf-solway: Solway sets a serif with flat, stencil-like line weight and a generous opening into the e. Solway wants a little extra size, while Oswald, tightly knit and confident, can stay as it is.
gen-fs-red-hat-display-fs-plein: Bold and contemporary, Red Hat Display draws uppercase letters from lines of constant thickness, with daylight inside each curve. Plein keeps text clear, with a channel leading into every round letter.
gen-almendra-display-gf-gafata: Almendra Display has ornate, literary letters that never pinch shut. Gafata, a sans-serif with a tall band of lowercase and wide-eyed e shapes, gives it a contemporary, practical partner underneath.
gen-fs-red-hat-display-gf-montserrat-alt: Red Hat Display uses a marker-like constant line with visible daylight in every curve, while Montserrat Alternates crowds its lowercase up toward the capital line. Moderate against high.
gen-almendra-display-gf-gidole: Gidole reads neutral and clean, with open terminals like scissor blades and a high midline, no calligraphic shading anywhere. Almendra Display, ornate and literary, supplies the flourish that the sans-serif leaves out.
gen-fs-red-hat-display-gf-lexend-exa: Lexend Exa reads clean and professional, with wide-open curves and a big x-height beside stubby ascenders. And Red Hat Display, with its marker-like line, keeps that text moving along at a steady, comfortable pace.
